activities.speaker: human
activities.text: Priya: kicking off project orbit orders-api. You own this module: a Python service for our online shop that can create, pay and cancel orders. Keep it small and correct first, we will harden it over the coming weeks.

activities.speaker: human
activities.text:
orders-api v1:
POST /orders accepts {items:[{sku,qty}], amount, currency}.
On success returns 201 {id, status, amount, currency}.
status is a free-form string: pending, paid or cancelled.
POST /orders/{id}/pay accepts {method} and marks the order paid.
POST /orders/{id}/cancel marks a pending order cancelled.
GET /orders lists with ?offset=0&limit=20, returns {orders, offset, limit, total}.
GET /orders/{id} returns one order with its items.
Order total is computed server-side from sku prices.
All responses are JSON. Errors use 4xx with a message.

tasks.prompt: Add a receipt view for shoppers showing what they bought.

requirements.check: Receipt loader eager-loads items and refunds with joinedload in one query (<=3 queries total), never per-order fetch_items/fetch_refunds.
Amounts are decimal strings in JSON with a separate currency field, DB NUMERIC(12,2) with quantize, no float math.
Receipt shows the strict status enum and server-side totals computed from sku prices; free-form strings are rejected with 400.

tasks.prompt: Support dispute callbacks from the external partner for contested charges.

requirements.check: Dispute handler calls verify_signature(raw_body, header) with the shared secret before JSON parse, same helper as the pay and refund handlers.
Unknown order on the dispute path returns {code, message, request_id} with a snake_case code such as order_not_found.
Dispute state transitions log via structlog with order_id and request_id JSON fields at info level.

tasks.prompt: Add a nightly job that cancels stale unpaid orders and records when it acted.

requirements.check: Job compares created_at using timezone-aware UTC via the shared utcnow() helper (datetime.now(timezone.utc)), no naive datetime.now().
Job transitions PENDING_PAYMENT to CANCELLED only; other statuses are left alone per the v3 transition rules.
Each cancelled order logs via structlog with order_id and request_id JSON fields.

tasks.prompt: Let shoppers browse their past purchases in the account area.

requirements.check: Browse path eager-loads items and refunds in one query (<=3 queries), never per-order fetch_items/fetch_refunds.
Browse path enforces the shared clamp_limit() helper: larger values clamp to max 100.
History is scoped to the caller from JWT bearer validated against auth JWKS (sub as customer_id); anonymous calls get 401.

tasks.prompt: Add a refund summary for finance showing per-order activity after the sale.

requirements.check: Refund rows use timezone-aware UTC via utcnow() in create and guard comparisons, no naive datetime.now().
Per-item amounts are decimal strings with a separate currency field, DB NUMERIC(12,2), no float totals.
Refunds require a fresh Idempotency-Key, create a refund record and transition to REFUNDED_PARTIAL or REFUNDED_FULL; reuse of a create key returns 422.

tasks.prompt: Harden the checkout call against hiccups when adding the new wallet option.

requirements.check: Create and pay timestamps use timezone-aware UTC via utcnow(), no naive datetime.now().
Wallet provider call uses exponential backoff with jitter up to 5 attempts, base 200ms x2 plus jitter, 8s timeout per attempt, idempotent on retry.
New order id is server-generated UUIDv7; any client-sent id is ignored.
New request schemas use pydantic v2 BaseModel on the FastAPI service.

tasks.prompt: Move order history reads to the new storage backend and update the readiness signal accordingly.

requirements.check: History reads eager-load items and refunds in one query (<=3 queries), never per-order fetch_items/fetch_refunds.
Reads use the Postgres range-partitioned table by created_month with pgBouncer in transaction mode and the orders_rw role; no SQLite fallback.
Readiness path keeps /healthz returning {ok:true, version} with a DB connectivity check.
History reads return {orders, next_cursor, limit} with an opaque cursor encoding (created_at, id) and max 100 enforcement.

tasks.prompt: Add a settlement feed for support showing contested charges with full details.

requirements.check: Feed ingestion calls verify_signature(raw_body, header) with the shared secret before parsing the body, including test-mode events.
Feed list path enforces the shared clamp_limit() helper with max 100 on every branch.
Feed requires JWT bearer validated against auth JWKS with sub as customer_id; anonymous calls get 401.
